usual_baseline: Rationale and timing of review usually above 90%. Medical review within 1 hour is poor: 20% [3273], 34% [3188][3281], 39% [3459], 44% [3380]. Content gaps: medication side effects 0% [3627], risk to self 5% [3380]. No review met all eight criteria [3627]. Independent reviews by an Approved Clinician often missing [3256].
fix_that_works: A seclusion review template in the documentation plus teaching: 95–100% [3128]. An integrated care pathway: MHC rule compliance from 3–100% to 69–100% [3040]. Education in secure LD wards: review within 1 hour 34% to 66%, medications 20% to 72% [3188]. Huddles and weekly meetings: consultant review within 24 hours from under 70% to over 90%, average seclusion 30 to 20 hours [3105].
fix_that_fails: Four PDSA cycles of proforma, email and teaching: 75% to 83%, minimal change on the SPC chart [3552]. Teaching and posters: side effects 0% to 19%, steps to end seclusion 25% to 23% [3627]. A previous audit led to no change [3273]. Just under half still monitored per guidelines [3105].
consultant_advice: Medical review documentation has been audited many times. Teaching alone gives small gains; a mandatory template works better. More useful: audit out-of-hours timing, Approved Clinician independent review [3256], seclusion room standards [3461], or seclusion duration.
